paper.title_en: Muon anomalous magnetic moment: Standard Model Theory
paper.abstract_en: This is a short review of the current status of the Standard Model calculation of the Muon <math display="inline" id="d1e2848" altimg="si1.svg"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>, based on the recently published White Paper. After a brief summary of the theoretically very well determined QED and electroweak contributions, the review focuses on the two main hadronic contributions, the vacuum polarization (HVP) and the light-by-light (HLbL), both for what concerns the lattice as well as the dispersive, data-driven determinations. In view of discrepancies in the data sets used for the dispersive determination of the HVP, the final theoretical value of the Muon <math display="inline" id="d1e2858" altimg="si1.svg"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> in the SM is based on the lattice value for the HVP contribution and an average of the lattice and dispersive determinations for the HLbL contribution. The review ends with a brief outlook on how to address two urgent challenges: (i) reduce the theory uncertainty by a factor four to match the experimental one; (ii) resolve the current puzzles affecting data-driven determinations of the HVP contribution.
